disproportionately

/dis-pruh-POR-shuh-nut-lee/ - the stress falls on POR · adverb

Hear It

What It Means

Disproportionately means out of proportion — to a degree far larger or smaller than the comparison it sits beside would justify.

Although seniors cast only a fifth of the votes, they appear disproportionately in the exit polls, filling nearly half the sample.

Example

The audit found that late fees fell disproportionately on the branch's smallest accounts: customers holding two percent of the deposits were paying forty percent of the penalties.

Two percent of the money, forty percent of the fees — the shares are wildly out of step, and disproportionately is the adverb that flags exactly that broken ratio. The word never judges an amount on its own; it always compares a share against the whole it came from.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

excessively: Excessively means more than is reasonable in itself; disproportionately always measures against something else — a share, a cause, a group's size — and finds the ratio wrong.

unduly: Unduly means more than is fair or warranted; unduly passes a quiet judgment, while disproportionately states the arithmetic — this piece is too big for that whole.

unevenly: Unevenly means without uniformity, in an irregular pattern; a coat of paint dries unevenly, but only when one share is wrong against another does disproportionately apply.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

proportionally: in step with the comparison it sits beside

evenly: in equal measures or shares

Where it sits · how far the share strays from its fair ratio

unevenly → disproportionately → overwhelmingly

unevenly vs. disproportionately: Unevenly is milder than disproportionately: uneven means the shares merely differ, while disproportionately means the difference has broken the ratio that fairness or arithmetic would predict.

overwhelmingly vs. disproportionately: Overwhelmingly outdoes disproportionately: a cost can fall disproportionately on renters at twice their fair share, but overwhelmingly means the imbalance has crowded out nearly everyone else's part.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-: not, the reverse of (Latin)

Root — proportion: the fitting ratio of part to whole (Latin pro portione, 'according to its share')

Suffix — -ate: having, marked by

Suffix — -ly: in the manner of

Put it together: The stack reads like a receipt: Latin pro portione, 'according to its share,' gives proportion; -ate makes the adjective; -ly makes the adverb; and dis- flips the whole thing over. At the bottom sits portio — Latin for a share or part — one of the busiest little roots English ever borrowed.

Use the root in a new word: apportion: The will named a cousin nobody trusted to apportion the estate, and the family braced itself.

Word Choice

analytical / pointed

Disproportionately is the adverb of audits and headlines, and it comes with homework: name the ratio, or the word is just noise. 'Fees fell disproportionately on small accounts' earns its keep only when the reader learns the shares. It runs both directions — a group can be disproportionately harmed or disproportionately rewarded.
